# QML Experimental Front-End Improvement Pass

## Overview

A full improvement pass over the experimental QML front-end
(`src/app/experimental/`, the `jtml_experimental` app built by plan 005 and
extended by plan 006), driven by the Qt QML skill suite: a structured review
(qt-qml-review), best-practice fixes (qt-qml), a UI/UX audit and polish
(qt-ui-design), Qt Quick Test coverage (qt-qml-test / qt-qml-test-run /
qt-cmake-project), and a performance baseline (qt-qml-profiler). The owner
explicitly sanctioned **breaking changes inside `src/app/experimental/`** —
it is a free sandbox. Everything else (widgets app, `src/view`, backend
seams, oracle, golden fixtures, packaging) is historical and untouched.

The plan is grounded in three research passes: repo/learning research (Qt
6.7.2 + QuickTest verified available in the pixi env; qmlformat/qmllint/
qmlprofiler/qmltestrunner all present), a spec-flow analysis of the QML view
layer (5 flows; 2 critical + 6 important + 6 minor gaps found), and direct
reading of all 5 QML files, the bridges, and the plan 005/006 docs.

---

## Problem Frame

Plan 005 shipped the app "functional, not polished" (its own words). The
view layer has never been reviewed against QML best practice, has zero
QML-side tests, no typography/accessibility system, and was never profiled.
The flow analysis additionally found view-layer state gaps with
data-integrity consequences (a stale pose table after optimizer runs, a
pending ML seed that silently overrides a manual arrangement, a pose-cell
commit contract that breaks under list virtualization). This pass fixes the
quality, UX, testability, and performance of the experimental front-end
while keeping the bridge/backend seams and the oracle-arbitrated parity
path intact.

Origin: direct owner request (2026-08-12) — "take a look at the
experimental qml stuff ... and have the myriad of qt qml skills while you
make a plan on improving it". Tracks selected by the owner: full pass
(review → fix → polish → tests → profile), UI/UX polish, QML test coverage,
performance profiling. Owner constraint: breaking changes allowed in
`src/app/experimental/`; historical code untouched.

---

## Requirements Trace

- R1. Structured review pass over all QML files (qt-qml-review: lint script
  + system qmllint + 6 parallel analysis agents) producing a triaged
  findings report in `docs/reviews/`.
- R2. Code-quality fixes per the qt-qml rules: component extraction
  (main.qml is ~1,020 lines of inline everything), Layout.* sizing
  compliance, binding hygiene, Theme token compliance, import cleanup.
- R3. UI/UX audit + polish per qt-ui-design: typography scale (TypeScale in
  the Theme singleton), keyboard navigation + visible focus, accessibility
  roles, contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for text, hit-target/sizing review.
- R4. View-layer testability: components take injected `required property`
  bridges instead of relying on context-property globals, so tests can
  inject fakes and the app fails loudly at load if a wiring is missed.
- R5. Qt Quick Test coverage (tst_Theme / tst_PoseCell / tst_SettingsPanel
  + view-flow tests) registered headless (offscreen platform, no VTK
  instantiation), following the repo test conventions.
- R6. Fix the view-layer state gaps found by the flow analysis: pose-table
  freshness (I1/I2), ML-seed-vs-manual-drag (I3), run-lock matrix
  completion (I4), Estimate enablement (I5), keyboard→bridge wiring (I6),
  and the pose-cell commit contract under virtualization (C1/C2).
- R7. Performance baseline via qmlprofiler on the 2D chrome (lists,
  dialogs, bindings; the VTK viewport is out of the profiler's scope) with
  the top hotspots fixed and re-documented.
- R8. Institutional capture: new `docs/solutions/` entries (Qt Quick Test
  recipe, qmllint gate, profiler recipe) + handoff update. Historical docs
  are not edited (owner constraint); the stale `MultiFilePicker.qml`
  reference in the 2026-08-11 conventions entry is noted, not rewritten.
- R9. Scope guard: only `src/app/experimental/**` + new test files +
  additive `test/CMakeLists.txt` registrations + new docs. The widgets app,
  `src/view`, backend seams, oracle/golden fixtures, and `packaging/` are
  untouched; `jtml.qml_parity_check` and all existing gates stay green.

---

## Scope Boundaries

- No changes outside `src/app/experimental/**` (QML + bridges + main.cpp +
  CMakeLists + qrc + qmldir), new test files, additive `test/CMakeLists.txt`
  registrations, and new docs. The owner constraint is absolute: historical
  code (widgets app, `src/view`, domain/services/coordinator/compute,
  oracle, golden fixtures, packaging) is not touched.
- No `qt_add_qml_module` conversion of the app target (see Key Technical
  Decisions — the qrc + qmldir approach stays; conversion is a separate
  future decision).
- No worker-thread move of the torch ML calls (GUI-thread freeze, M4): it
  is documented and measured in U7, not fixed.
- No shell-level unsaved-changes indicator (M6): deferred.
- No changes to the backend seams' public APIs (bridges stay pass-throughs;
  all behavior stays in the seams).
- The render-thread contract (`QmlVtkRenderer` + `ExperimentalScene`) is
  unchanged; the pass does not touch VTK pipeline code.

### Deferred to Follow-Up Work

- `qt_add_qml_module` conversion + QML language-server integration for the
  app (needs care with the render-smoke target that loads `qrc:/renderer.qml`
  — separate gated cut).
- Full-window redesign / layout overhaul beyond token-level polish (the
  pass keeps the existing shell layout).
- Shell-level dirty indicator, torch worker-thread move, RTL/localization
  support (English-only tool, single locale).

---

## Context & Research

### Relevant Code and Patterns

- `src/app/experimental/main.qml` (~1,020 lines) — the shell: toolbar,
  study lists, ML strip, viewport, run bar, 8 FileDialogs + 2 custom
  dialogs; 5 `Connections` blocks to the bridges (main.qml:417-461).
- `src/app/experimental/SettingsPanel.qml` — settings form with inline
  `component` definitions (RangeField/IntField/CostVariantCombo); does NOT
  import the theme module (hardcodes `#cfd3da`/`#8b929c` where
  `Theme.fg`/`Theme.fgMuted` exist).
- `src/app/experimental/PoseCell.qml` — editable pose cell; commit at
  `onEditingFinished` reads `studyBridge.primaryModelIndex` at commit time
  (C2) and restores on failed commit with a plain assignment that
  permanently kills the `storedValue` binding (C1).
- `src/app/experimental/Theme.qml` + `qmldir` — singleton palette; dirty-
  badge hexes duplicated in main.qml:221-227 and SettingsPanel (M2);
  `Theme.border` unused; no type scale.
- `src/app/experimental/{AppBridge,StudyBridge,SettingsBridge,OptimizerBridge,MlBridge,PoseBridge,FileDialogBridge}.h/.cpp` —
  thin QObject adapters (thinness rule), registered as root-context
  properties in `main.cpp`. Existing headless bridge tests:
  `jtml.experimental_selection`, `jtml.experimental_settings`,
  `jtml.experimental_optimizer_gate`, `jtml.experimental_ml_bridge`,
  `jtml.experimental_pose_bridge`.
- Test conventions: flat `test/CMakeLists.txt`, `jtml.<name>` test names,
  `LABELS "headless"` + repo-root `WORKING_DIRECTORY`, Q_OBJECT headers in
  the `add_executable` source list (AUTOMOC), block-scoped
  `find_package(Qt6 COMPONENTS ...)` (precedent:
  `jtml_test_qml_render_smoke` block), rpath recipe.
- QML smoke precedent: `test/oracle/qml_render_smoke.cpp` + `renderer.qrc`
  (xcb, `LABELS "oracle;render"`).

### Institutional Learnings

- `docs/solutions/conventions/jtml-qml-experimental-frontend-2026-08-11.md`
  — the app charter: render-thread contract (copy scene state on the GUI
  thread, capture by value), versionless imports, Theme singleton rules
  (`pragma Singleton` + `qmldir`), Material Dark choice, Dialog-based
  secondary surfaces. **Note: this entry references a `MultiFilePicker.qml`
  that no longer exists (superseded by `FileDialogBridge`) — historical
  entry, not edited; the drift is noted in U8's new entry.**
- `docs/solutions/ui-bugs/jtml-qml-model-pose-sync-queued-functor-never-delivered-2026-08-11.md`
  — direct by-value signal emits work; queued `invokeMethod` functors
  silently fail. Any new view→bridge signaling uses signal emits.
- `docs/solutions/tooling-decisions/jtml-rendering-runtime-xcb-qvtk-2026-08-10.md`
  — xcb-only rendering; grabWindow-only capture; QML tests must not
  instantiate VTK/GL.
- `docs/solutions/conventions/jtml-testability-and-cmake-conventions-2026-08-07.md`
  — AUTOMOC header-in-sources rule, explicit source lists, rpath recipe.
- `docs/solutions/conventions/jtml-mainscreen-decomposition-patterns-2026-08-10.md`
  — selection-command traps (the delegate-selection contract sidesteps
  them deliberately), torch `#undef slots` include ordering.
- qmllint / Qt Quick Test / qmlprofiler are **uncaptured territory** in
  `docs/solutions/` — the pass captures the recipes (U8).

### External References

- The Qt QML skill suite (authoritative, version-aware): qt-qml (rules),
  qt-qml-review (lint + agent checklists), qt-ui-design (WCAG 2.2, modular
  scale), qt-qml-test (47 testing rules), qt-qml-test-run, qt-qml-profiler
  (trace parser + anti-pattern catalogue), qt-cmake-project (Qt 6 CMake
  API rules). The skills are the version-specific external guidance; no
  further external research was dispatched.
- Verified in the pixi env: Qt 6.7.2 with `Qt6QuickTestConfig.cmake`,
  `qmltestrunner`, `libqoffscreen.so`, `qmlformat`, `qmllint`,
  `qmlprofiler` — headless QuickTest + lint + profiling are all runnable.

---

## Key Technical Decisions

| # | Decision | Rationale |
|---|----------|-----------|
| D1 | **Property injection for testability:** components declare `required property var <bridge>` (same names as today's context properties), wired explicitly in `main.qml`. | Tests inject fakes; a missed wiring fails loudly at load instead of silently falling back to context properties (which would make tests pass against real bridges). Answers flow question Q9. |
| D2 | **PoseCell commit contract:** capture `(frameRow, axisIndex, primaryModelIndex)` when editing starts; commit against the captured values on `editingFinished`; failed commits restore the display through a re-sync `Binding` (or `Qt.binding`), never a one-shot assignment. | Fixes C1 (wrong-row commit under recycling) and C2 (commit-to-new-primary on mid-edit selection change) and the binding-kill regression. Answers Q1. |
| D3 | **Single pose-table refresh owner:** `PoseBridge` hooks `runStateChanged` (completed) and `viewerPoseApplied`/`scenePoseChanged` and refreshes the table model. | One owner, no double-refresh; fixes I1/I2 (stale table after runs and viewer drags). Answers Q2. |
| D4 | **ML seed invalidation:** any manual pose write (viewer drag or pose-table edit) on the seeded frame+model drops the pending ML seed. | Prevents the optimizer silently overriding the user's final arrangement (I3). Answers Q3. |
| D5 | **Full run-lock matrix:** extend the existing `!optimizerBridge.running` lock to the Black-silhouette checkbox, the Fem/Tib buttons, and viewport interaction (`enabled: false` on the renderer — blocks mouse events). | Completes the DisableAll mirror (I4); drags during a run are a semantic clobber. Answers Q4. |
| D6 | **Estimate enablement:** add `mlBridge.hasSegmentModel` to the Estimate button binding + a hint label when disabled. | Matches AE4 degradation and the Segment button's pattern (I5). Answers Q5. |
| D7 | **Keyboard contract:** frame list wires `onCurrentIndexChanged → studyBridge.setCurrentFrame` (single source of truth; list highlight + bridge can't diverge); model list toggles on Space/Enter; rows are focusable (`activeFocusOnTab`), ListView handles Up/Down; visible focus indicator bound to `activeFocus`. | Fixes I6 and satisfies qt-ui-design keyboard requirements. Answers Q6. |

# QML Experimental Front-End Improvement Pass

## Overview

A full improvement pass over the experimental QML front-end
(`src/app/experimental/`, the `jtml_experimental` app built by plan 005 and
extended by plan 006), driven by the Qt QML skill suite: a structured review
(qt-qml-review), best-practice fixes (qt-qml), a UI/UX audit and polish
(qt-ui-design), Qt Quick Test coverage (qt-qml-test / qt-qml-test-run /
qt-cmake-project), and a performance baseline (qt-qml-profiler). The owner
explicitly sanctioned **breaking changes inside `src/app/experimental/`** —
it is a free sandbox. Everything else (widgets app, `src/view`, backend
seams, oracle, golden fixtures, packaging) is historical and untouched.

The plan is grounded in three research passes: repo/learning research (Qt
6.7.2 + QuickTest verified available in the pixi env; qmlformat/qmllint/
qmlprofiler/qmltestrunner all present), a spec-flow analysis of the QML view
layer (5 flows; 2 critical + 6 important + 6 minor gaps found), and direct
reading of all 5 QML files, the bridges, and the plan 005/006 docs.

---

## Problem Frame

Plan 005 shipped the app "functional, not polished" (its own words). The
view layer has never been reviewed against QML best practice, has zero
QML-side tests, no typography/accessibility system, and was never profiled.
The flow analysis additionally found view-layer state gaps with
data-integrity consequences (a stale pose table after optimizer runs, a
pending ML seed that silently overrides a manual arrangement, a pose-cell
commit contract that breaks under list virtualization). This pass fixes the
quality, UX, testability, and performance of the experimental front-end
while keeping the bridge/backend seams and the oracle-arbitrated parity
path intact.

Origin: direct owner request (2026-08-12) — "take a look at the
experimental qml stuff ... and have the myriad of qt qml skills while you
make a plan on improving it". Tracks selected by the owner: full pass
(review → fix → polish → tests → profile), UI/UX polish, QML test coverage,
performance profiling. Owner constraint: breaking changes allowed in
`src/app/experimental/`; historical code untouched.

---

## Requirements Trace

- R1. Structured review pass over all QML files (qt-qml-review: lint script
  + system qmllint + 6 parallel analysis agents) producing a triaged
  findings report in `docs/reviews/`.
- R2. Code-quality fixes per the qt-qml rules: component extraction
  (main.qml is ~1,020 lines of inline everything), Layout.* sizing
  compliance, binding hygiene, Theme token compliance, import cleanup.
- R3. UI/UX audit + polish per qt-ui-design: typography scale (TypeScale in
  the Theme singleton), keyboard navigation + visible focus, accessibility
  roles, contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for text, hit-target/sizing review.
- R4. View-layer testability: components take injected `required property`
  bridges instead of relying on context-property globals, so tests can
  inject fakes and the app fails loudly at load if a wiring is missed.
- R5. Qt Quick Test coverage (tst_Theme / tst_PoseCell / tst_SettingsPanel
  + view-flow tests) registered headless (offscreen platform, no VTK
  instantiation), following the repo test conventions.
- R6. Fix the view-layer state gaps found by the flow analysis: pose-table
  freshness (I1/I2), ML-seed-vs-manual-drag (I3), run-lock matrix
  completion (I4), Estimate enablement (I5), keyboard→bridge wiring (I6),
  and the pose-cell commit contract under virtualization (C1/C2).
- R7. Performance baseline via qmlprofiler on the 2D chrome (lists,
  dialogs, bindings; the VTK viewport is out of the profiler's scope) with
  the top hotspots fixed and re-documented.
- R8. Institutional capture: new `docs/solutions/` entries (Qt Quick Test
  recipe, qmllint gate, profiler recipe) + handoff update. Historical docs
  are not edited (owner constraint); the stale `MultiFilePicker.qml`
  reference in the 2026-08-11 conventions entry is noted, not rewritten.
- R9. Scope guard: only `src/app/experimental/**` + new test files +
  additive `test/CMakeLists.txt` registrations + new docs. The widgets app,
  `src/view`, backend seams, oracle/golden fixtures, and `packaging/` are
  untouched; `jtml.qml_parity_check` and all existing gates stay green.

---

## Scope Boundaries

- No changes outside `src/app/experimental/**` (QML + bridges + main.cpp +

  future decision).
- No worker-thread move of the torch ML calls (GUI-thread freeze, M4): it
  is documented and measured in U7, not fixed.
- No shell-level unsaved-changes indicator (M6): deferred.
- No changes to the backend seams' public APIs (bridges stay pass-throughs;
  all behavior stays in the seams).
- The render-thread contract (`QmlVtkRenderer` + `ExperimentalScene`) is
  unchanged; the pass does not touch VTK pipeline code.

### Deferred to Follow-Up Work

- `qt_add_qml_module` conversion + QML language-server integration for the

| D1 | **Property injection for testability:** components declare `required property var <bridge>` (same names as today's context properties), wired explicitly in `main.qml`. | Tests inject fakes; a missed wiring fails loudly at load instead of silently falling back to context properties (which would make tests pass against real bridges). Answers flow question Q9. |
| D2 | **PoseCell commit contract:** capture `(frameRow, axisIndex, primaryModelIndex)` when editing starts; commit against the captured values on `editingFinished`; failed commits restore the display through a re-sync `Binding` (or `Qt.binding`), never a one-shot assignment. | Fixes C1 (wrong-row commit under recycling) and C2 (commit-to-new-primary on mid-edit selection change) and the binding-kill regression. Answers Q1. |
| D3 | **Single pose-table refresh owner:** `PoseBridge` hooks `runStateChanged` (completed) and `viewerPoseApplied`/`scenePoseChanged` and refreshes the table model. | One owner, no double-refresh; fixes I1/I2 (stale table after runs and viewer drags). Answers Q2. |
| D4 | **ML seed invalidation:** any manual pose write (viewer drag or pose-table edit) on the seeded frame+model drops the pending ML seed. | Prevents the optimizer silently overriding the user's final arrangement (I3). Answers Q3. |

Answers Q4. |

Answers Q6. |

```

  main.qml            → bootstrap only: Window + toolbar + region composition
                        + FileDialogs (one owner per dialog) + message/replace
                        dialogs. Target ≤ ~300 lines.
  Theme.qml           → palette tokens + TypeScale roles (caption/label/body/h2)
  StudyPanel.qml      → frame list + model list + selection label (new)
  MlStrip.qml         → ML pickers/buttons/status labels (extracted from main.qml)

  SettingsPanel.qml   → existing; gains the theme import + injected settingsBridge
  PosesTable.qml      → the pose table (ScrollView + rows) extracted from the
                        PosesDialog body (new; U5 virtualizes it)
  PosesDialog.qml     → the Poses dialog shell (header, actions, table, message)
  PoseCell.qml        → existing; reworked commit contract (D2)
  renderer.qml        → unchanged (smoke scene)
```

### Component wiring contract (extraction constraints from the flow analysis)

- **Single-owner `Connections` per bridge:** the 5 glue blocks in main.qml
  (417-461) move to the component that owns the surface they feed
  (viewport glue stays in the center-panel composition; dialog glue in the
  dialog components). No component creates a second `Connections` to a
  bridge the root already observes.
- **The `Qt.callLater` deferral in `onDatasetChanged` (main.qml:421-424)
  must survive extraction** — it exists to outlast the list-model swap
  (`clearDataset` deletes the old model instance).
- **The viewport id is referenced from the toolbar, 4 glue blocks, and the
  ML strip** — the center region is a component exposing
  `property alias viewport`, never `findChild`.
- **The Run button closes both edit dialogs (main.qml:980-981)** — dialogs
  expose `open()`/`close()` or stay root-owned; the run bar does not reach
  into dialog internals.
- Every new component file is registered in `qmldir` (engine-root
  documents cannot use inline components — the documented PoseCell
  limitation) and listed in `resources.qrc`.

The six angles answer the question — "what are the next layers of deeper exploration?" — with a converging, and mildly surprising, picture: the highest-leverage next work is **neither a new algorithm nor a new architecture — it is measurement infrastructure**. And the cost path that gate protects — the R15 load-bearing DIRECT_DILATION family — contains seven documented live bugs with zero metric-math test coverage (angles 01 + 05). Every other research direction's verdict must land on instruments that do not yet exist.

Concretely: (a) add a production-shaped multi-stage oracle variant (cumulative 20k→25k→30k→35k, dilation 6/4/1 or 6/3/1 pending the contradiction below, z opened to ±15 in leaf, tibia-after-femur, sym_trap disambiguation) so the weak axis is observed through the real stage loop (angle 06), and (b) build the metric-ablation harness with its z-profile probe — sweep z across ±15 mm at truth pose and plot the cost curve per variant (angle 01 calls this "the single most informative new experiment"). Together these convert the repo's biggest unknown into a measured quantity, and they make every later decision (cost-variant ranking, weight calibration, dilation-schedule ablation, DIRECT-variant verdicts, ML initializer quality) adjudicable.

The algorithm-improvement work then becomes cheap and evidence-gated. The DIRECT core (src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp) is a faithful Jones-1993 with effectively epsilon=0 — the one configuration the 25-years survey documents as pathological for expensive costs, because it over-refines suboptimal local minima and can burn much of the 20k trunk budget before the branch stage sees fresh dilation (angle 02, https://websites.umich.edu/~mdolaboratory/pdf/Jones2020a.pdf). The highest-evidence, lowest-risk fix is refinement control (epsilon / delta-limit / DIRECT-restart's adaptive epsilon), then the DIRECT-l infinity-norm size measure, then two-step Pareto (DIRECT-GL) — each gated by a headless analytic battery before any GPU spend, and by the oracle afterward. On the cost side, the chamfer (DistanceMapMetric) is the only z-sensitive term in the default cost and its blend weight is accidental; the geometric priors at weight 1 are ~0.01–0.3% of the base cost — effectively inert — and sym_trap's 75/500 weights are the only ones in the right scale (angle 01). The repo's documented deviation from the D.R.E.C.T. paper (dilating *both* sides of the comparison vs the paper's dilation-pyramid-on-fluoro-edge) has never been ablated — and one live bug (bug-4, the always-Trunk stage guard) currently makes the paper-style path unreachable (angle 01).

The architectural verdicts are equally clear. **QML: NO-GO now** — it is a plan-005-scale rewrite (Path A) whose payoff is styling, none of the current problems are QML problems, the ecosystem is QWidgets-first (ParaView, 3D Slicer, MITK, ImFusion), and the Slicer maintainer's warning ("plan extra time for testing and development at each Qt or VTK release") is a small-lab cost the repo cannot absorb quietly; the correct action is a one-line decision record replacing the "QML-swappable later" comment (angle 04). **Compute: sync-bound, not kernel-bound** — ~15 kernel launches and ~5 synchronous D2H pipeline drains per evaluation, ~175k drains per 35k-eval frame; measure first with the already-wired nvtx dep, then remove per-eval syncs (angle 05). **Determinism is better than the docs claim**: every reduction in the DIRECT_DILATION path is int-atomic (order-independent, value-deterministic); only the DRR float atomicAdd (never called by the cost path) is order-nondeterministic — so the 6.31 mm gap is cross-machine float/FMA divergence + DIRECT chaos + a real production-vs-oracle backface-culling config difference, not atomic ordering (angle 05). **The ML pathway's right shape is segmentation→initializer→DIRECT** — the repo's DIRECT stage is verbatim the published, independently validated stage 3 of the lab's own Jensen 2023 pipeline (0.8/0.5/2.6 mm and 0.5–1.7° vs RSA/mocap); ML should be invested in as an *initializer* with renderer-generated synthetic labels (no clinical annotation needed), never as an end-to-end pose regressor, and the oracle must gate the *refined* pose, not raw estimator output (angle 03).

Recommended course of action, in order: (1) fix the seven live bugs and delete the dead duplicate chamfer term with pin-first tests — days of work, unpoisons every downstream measurement (angles 01, 05); (2) build the metric-ablation harness with the z-profile probe, headless first (angle 01); (3) add the production-shaped multi-stage oracle variant, calibrate the IoU threshold to a cross-GPU noise floor, and wire a self-hosted gpu-labeled CI runner (angle 06) — the highest-leverage single direction; (4) then run the DIRECT variant switch and the cost-family z remedies, each oracle-adjudicated (angles 02, 01); (5) sequence the ML initializer pathway after the oracle can measure refined poses, and expand fixtures toward tibia and biplane for the z ceiling (angles 03, 06); (6) defer QML, and write the intended-purpose statement + SOUP inventory now — regulatory posture is a written decision, and AGPL is not a shield (angle 06).

** The z weak axis is the load-bearing research problem — and the current oracle cannot see it
Consolidated from angles 01, 02, 03, 06. Convergence: five independent sources document monoplane depth as the hardest axis for every method family — Penney 1998 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9845314/), Yamazaki 2004 (https://researchr.org/publication/YamazakiWNSTYT04), DAMN's 25 mm out-of-plane vs 0.75 mm in-plane (https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0270596), Jensen 2023's 2.6 mm ML (largest DOF error) (https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2205.00057), Veriserum's dual-plane motivation ("superior out-of-plane accuracy", https://arxiv.org/html/2509.05483). The repo-side mechanism is geometric: a ±15 mm z shift at ~1.1 m source distance changes magnification <1%, far inside the 6 px dilation tolerance, so dilated overlap is nearly flat in z (angle 01, derived from baseline.json + assumed SID, medium confidence on the arithmetic). The repo's own z estimator (area-ratio z = -pd·sqrt(sum_proj/sum_seg), src/services/implant_estimator.cpp) is a deterministic readout of the same weak signal; expecting any method — learned or classical — to fix monoplane z is unrealistic (angles 01, 03, 06 agree). ** The R15 load-bearing cost path contains 7 live bugs, zero metric-math tests, and an uncalibrated blend — it is the foundation that must be cleaned first
Consolidated from angles 01 and 05. Angle 01 found in the registered variants: bug-1 uninitialized `min_dist` read (UB) in DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT (src/compute/DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:155-169); bug-2 Y_dist ≡ X_dist copy-paste making the Y_TRANS constraint a no-op (141-148 vs 133-139); bug-3 sym_trap builds the tibia transform with x replaced by z, corrupting varus/valgus and pole distance (src/compute/sym_trap_function.cpp:104-108); bug-4 the always-true stage guard in CostFunctionManager makes DIRECT_DILATION_T1's non-trunk path unreachable (src/compute/CostFunctionManager.cpp:63-64). Angle 05 found in the active cost path: DistanceMapMetric_Kernel's broken index formula (`blockIdx.y + gridDim.x + blockIdx.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`, src/compute/distance_map_metric.cu:20) — a subtle bias in the trunk cost every evaluation; ImplantMahfouzMetric's pointer-vs-value denominator check (`if (pixel_score_ != 0)` — always true, so a zero denominator divides by zero, src/compute/implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:346,464) plus a double→int atomicAdd truncation; and CurvatureHeatmapMetric as a stub that returns 0 without launching its kernel (curvature_hausdorf_metric.cu:41-76). Test coverage: test/unit/test_cost_function.cpp covers only the parameter registry — zero metric math (angle 01). The metrics also mutate the rendered image in place, so composition only works by mutation ordering (angle 05). The documented "DIFFERENT FROM JTA PAPER" symmetric-dilation deviation (5 cost files) is untested by design decision, not evidence (angle 01). The scale finding compounds everything: overlap terms are O(10³–10⁴) while the chamfer mean is O(1–10) and the SAME_Z/pole priors at weight 1 are ~0.01–0.3% of base cost — the blend weights are accidental, and sym_trap's 75/500 are the only calibrated ones (angle 01).

** The DIRECT core is faithful-but-unmodernized; refinement control — not a new algorithm — is the highest-evidence optimizer upgrade
Angle 02 (with refs/ Jones 1993 read): the repo implements Jones-1993's lower-right convex hull with effectively epsilon=0, L2 size measure, single-largest-denormalized-side trisection, no Lipschitz estimation, no restart, no local refinement. The 25-years survey (https://websites.umich.edu/~mdolaboratory/pdf/Jones2020a.pdf) documents epsilon=0's excessive-local-refinement pathology (Shubert: >10,000 evals at 0.01% accuracy with epsilon=0 vs 2933 with 1e-4), and the 2022 study's headline for expensive costs: "when objective functions are expensive, local refinement reduction techniques improve performance" (https://epublications.vu.lt/object/elaba:143490244/143490244.pdf) — the GPU-DRR case exactly. Dimensionality is on the repo's side (6D is DIRECT's sweet spot; deterministic algorithms excel in low dimensions, https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.05759). Compounding with angle 05: the per-eval cost is sync-dominated (~5 D2H drains/eval), so every evaluation is expensive in wall-clock terms — the precise regime where refinement control pays. Compounding with angle 03: a good ML initializer narrows the search box, directly mitigating the same over-refinement risk. The trunk→2×branch→leaf stage design is the documented multistage/zoom family pattern (Jones-2001 revision, MrDIRECT, HD-DIRECT, DIRECT-JTA itself) and is well-posed *provided* each stage's budget is not squandered (angle 02). The one configuration deviation with no literature counterpart — splitting by largest *denormalized* side — is an implicit dimension weighting (z-heavy) that should be kept and documented (angle 02; NLopt NOSCAL is the only analogue). Noisy-DIRECT (plural sampling) is explicitly out of scope at this budget (angle 02) — and angle 05 confirms the cost is deterministic per machine, so stochastic machinery is moot.

** Determinism is better than the docs claim — and the doc contradiction is itself a finding
